report: Refreshed source review of the complete claim, sole ordinary debug-configured validate_stash_id association, four ordinary tests, and explicit service_spec TODO. Allocating-stash interpretation is supported by make_ptr/make_slice stamping identity and both Index implementations checking identity in debug configurations plus type on retrieval. cross_stash_ptr_same_type_panics_in_debug and cross_stash_slice_panics_in_debug require the identity-mismatch panic despite corresponding indexes and equal element types; release executions have no rejection assertion and do not establish release enforcement. For explicit boundary copying, Stashed::copy_into delegates to StashCopy; Ptr recursively copies its source pointee before target allocation and Slice recursively copies elements before target slice allocation. copy_into_compound reads both nested handles exclusively through the target and asserts distinct Point values; copy_into_with_slice asserts both target elements. These visible assertions catch retained foreign handles under debug checks and wrong copy values. Recaptured the Point fixture dependency. Compared the current complete implementation against the previously reviewed snapshot: the only delta replaces the scalar collision count debug assertion with count!=1 continue before read_one, with an explanatory safety comment. The new guard skips incompatible slice entries while preserving destination allocation, identity stamping and recursive copy behavior; it does not close the compiler-wide ownership evidence gap. Current claim and all associated test bodies were reassessed. The service_spec TODO still explicitly defers complete equal/unequal-type access evidence, nested pointer/slice coverage and completed-query destination-only output walking. Its prerequisites remain comprehensive associated boundary tests and representative checked output traversals that consult neither source CST nor imported query stashes. Accepted TODO does not claim those cases implemented; no N/A evidence exists. Personally ran review start/read, inspected fresh inputs and the source delta, and recorded this report; no behavioral tests or workspace build were personally run. Coordinator reports 331 sage-meta functional tests, 46 stash tests and workspace build passing, separately from this source assessment. No source edits required.
